    92	Build an audio truth map by probing every segment:
    93	- `ffprobe` → `has_audio`, `nb_streams`
    94	- `audio_produce(provider=elevenlabs, mode=speech2text, model=scribe_v2)` → canonical speech analysis. Returns `transcript_file` with word-level timestamps. This is the ONLY speech-detection tool.
    95	- `video-editor__analyze_audio` → loudness/tempo only (LUFS, true_peak, BPM). Not for transcripts.
    96	- `analyze_file_content` → supporting visual check for on-camera speaking, burned-in text cards.
    97	
    98	Per-segment truth map: `has_audio`, `audio_source` (co-gen / audio_list_tts / audio_list_music / silent / user_upload), `embedded_speech`, `embedded_music`, `speech_transcript_file`.
    99	
   100	**Decision gates**:
   101	- `embedded_speech=true` → BLOCKED from adding same speech as separate track
   102	- `embedded_music=true` → BLOCKED from adding separate BGM without explicit intent
   103	- `silent` → safe to add any layers
   104	- `co-gen SFX only` → safe to add VO; duck segment volume
   105	- **Conflict** (embedded speech + orphan TTS both exist): classify by speaker visibility — on-screen → keep co-gen; off-screen narration → keep TTS. Re-plan, don't just block.
   106	- **Lipsync** (`audio_list` + `sound: "on"`): TTS is baked into video. No separate VO track for same lines. Duration mismatch >200ms → rebuild upstream.
   107	- **Nonzero embedded-speech overlap hard stop**: If STT detects speech in a video clip and any separate speech clip overlaps that time window, adding the separate speech clip is BLOCKED unless the transcript is intentionally different dialogue and the mix plan explicitly calls for simultaneous speakers. Lowering embedded speech to `0.08`, `0.05`, or any other "nearly muted" value is still audio doubling and is BLOCKED.
   108	- **Lipsync/audio_list priority**: When the segment lineage is `audio_list_tts` or visible on-camera sync speech, the embedded audio is the intended speech source after generation. Do not add the same TTS/VO again in assembly. If STT confirms the embedded transcript matches closely enough, keep the segment audio at dialogue volume. If STT shows the generated video says different words from the intended line, do not cover it with the correct VO; regenerate with the correct `audio_list`/exact dialogue contract, or ask for a strategy change before treating the shot as silent B-roll.
   109	- **Fail closed**: If speech analysis fails and the doubling decision depends on it, stop.
   110	
   111	### 2. Transitions & Timeline
   112	
   113	- Crossfade (500–750ms) for continuous performance; cut for scene changes. See `references/editing-rhythm-design.md`.
   114	- Fade and crossfade are mutually exclusive at same cut point.
   115	- Duration: `actual = Σ(segment_durations) − Σ(crossfade_ms)`. Verify with `get_file_info` after render (±2s).
   116	- Audio `start_ms` = sum of preceding clips' **output** durations. Output duration = `(out_ms − in_ms) / speed`.
   117	- All `_ms` suffix — no frame-based fields.
   118	
   119	### 3. Volume Mixing
   120	
   121	| Priority | Layer | Volume Rule |
   122	|:--------:|-------|-------------|
   123	| P1 | VO / narration | 1.0, `dbfs: -16` — never masked |
   124	| P2 | On-screen dialogue (co-gen/lipsync) | 1.0 — duck BGM, never duck this |
   125	| P3 | Key SFX (co-gen) | ≥ 0.6 — duck only under P1 |
   126	| P4 | Ambient (co-gen) | 0.3–0.5 under VO |
   127	| P5 | BGM | 0.08–0.15 under VO; 0.20–0.30 in gaps; ≤0.25 standalone |
   128	
   129	Per-segment mixing: characterize embedded audio type (dialogue/SFX/ambience) via `analyze_audio` + `analyze_file_content`, then set volume accordingly. Do not apply flat volume across all segments.
   130	
   131	Speech overlap rule: volume ducking is for SFX, ambience, and BGM under VO. It is not a repair for wrong or duplicate speech. When the video clip contains embedded speech, assembly should normally keep that speech and suppress the separate VO/TTS track, especially for `audio_list_tts` or visible on-camera sync speech. `volume > 0` on a speech-bearing video clip plus overlapping separate speech is allowed only for intentional multi-speaker dialogue that is explicitly in the script. Otherwise it is BLOCKED.
   132	
   133	### 4. VO Production
   134	
   135	- Route: `provider=elevenlabs`, `mode=text2speech`, `model=eleven_v3`. Voice catalog in `references/vo-design-principles.md` Section 6.
   136	- One call per spoken line (no batch mode).
   137	- **Duration gate**: `voiceover_duration <= (total_video_duration - voiceover_start_time)`. Overflow → shorten text and regenerate, or extend visuals.
   138	- **Source-window gate**: `source.out_ms - source.in_ms` must cover full VO. Shorter by >200ms with speech remaining → BLOCKED.
   139	- **Subtitle source**: Use `subtitle_file` (alignment JSON) from `audio_produce`. Never use audio MP3/WAV as subtitle source. No `subtitle_file` → only coarse approximate captions.
   140	- **Manual spoken-caption fallback is exceptional, not normal**: If `subtitle_file` exists, do not rewrite the same spoken line as manual `kind=text` subtitles. The only allowed fallback case is: no stable subtitle render path is available, no better timed subtitle asset exists, and the user can accept approximate captions.
   141	- **Subtitle dedup**: Check for existing burned-in subtitles/text cards via `analyze_file_content`; suppress caption where video already has readable text.
   142	- **Subtitle/text design**: Follow `references/video-editor-tool-guide.md` for motion, safe areas, fonts, placement.
   143	- **Text overlay fit is a hard preflight**: Before using manual `kind=text`, confirm the line fits the protected stage after font size, border, shadow, and box padding are considered. If it does not fit, split cues first; only then reduce styling weight.
   144	- **Render-safe copy by default**: Ordinary subtitles should use plain render-safe wording and punctuation. Remove unnecessary emoji / decorative symbols rather than trying to force them through styling.
   145	- Generic TTS ≠ identity-preserving dub — never substitute without user acknowledgement.
   146	- If VO fails repeatedly, surface it — don't silently ship music-only.
   147	
   148	### 5. BGM Production
   149	
   150	- **Timing modes**: Video-first (default — generate BGM after all segments, use `composition_plan`), Music-first (BGM drives video via `audio_list`), Independent (parallel, prompt mode).
   151	- Duration must exactly match visual timeline. Calculate from actual segment durations.
   152	- `text_to_music`: `prompt` mode or `composition_plan` mode (mutually exclusive). Composition plan sections ≥3000ms each.
   153	- No copyrighted references in music prompts.
   154	- **Adaptive strategy**: Dense sound-on → sectional BGM, not wall-to-wall. BGM bridges gaps.
   155	- If visual rhythm changed after re-gen, existing BGM likely misaligns → re-generate video-first.
   156	- BGM planned but file missing → BLOCKED. Do not silently drop planned BGM.
   157	
   158	### 6. Duration Enforcement & Non-Generative Edits
   159	
   160	- Verify segment durations via ffprobe. Trim overlong with `in_ms`/`out_ms`. Total must match target ±1s.
   161	- Speed changes: apply `speed` on full source range.
   162	- Available: trim, speed, crop, scale, volume, fade, keyframe animation (`scale_kf`, `speed_kf`, `opacity_kf`, `x_kf`, `y_kf`).
   163	- Audio-only editing (no video tracks) → output `.aac`.
   164	
   165	### 7. Cover Image (after assembly, before delivery)
   166	
   167	- Priority: existing key frame / style_ref > extracted frame from ~1–2s > generated via `image_generate`.
   168	- Hard-reject near-black, blurred, transitional frames.
   169	- Bake into MP4 as first 1–3 frames (silent). Skip if dialogue starts at 0s.
   170	
   171	### 8. Reassembly & Integrity
   172	
   173	- Always from original individual segments, never from rendered composite.
   174	- Preserve co-gen audio at volume 1.0 unless explicitly muted.
   175	- Post-render: verify duration via ffprobe. Delta >2s → structural problem, rebuild (don't trim composite).
   176	- Every planned shot must appear in edit spec — no silent omissions.
   177	
   178	### 9. Interruption Recovery
   179	
   180	- Inventory surviving assets, reuse them.
   181	- Preserve successful parameter patterns. Pick up from failure point.
   182	- Inform user what survived and what remains.
   183	
   184	---
   185	
   186	# Tools
   187	
   188	Tools are provided at runtime. This skill uses:
   189	- `execute_edit_video` — timeline assembly, transitions, audio mixing, non-generative edits
   190	- `audio_produce` — TTS/VO generation + speech2text analysis
   191	- `text_to_music` — BGM generation (prompt or composition_plan)
   192	- `image_generate` — cover image (fallback only)
   193	- `get_file_info` — file info / duration verification
   194	- `ffprobe` — media probe (duration, resolution, fps)
   195	
   196	For edit-spec structure, DSL patterns, text/subtitle design, and common errors, see `references/video-editor-tool-guide.md`.

Aqui está — **~15s, 9:16**, três perspectivas cinematográficas em crossfade suave:

1. **Plano geral → close** — o estúdio da ARP Produções revelado com chuva na janela, ela ao microfone com a mão no peito
2. **Plano médio** — caminhando ao redor do microfone, gestos expressivos, neon azul no chão
3. **Close emocional** — lágrimas, rosto iluminado pelo neon, chuva ao fundo em bokeh

A BGM de piano melancólico + strings corre por baixo com o áudio ambiente co-gerado nas três cenas — chuva, atmosfera de estúdio. Tudo na estética Silent Hearts. Quer ajustar alguma cena, o ritmo dos cortes ou a música?

skills_metadata.name: assembly-skill
skills_metadata.description: Post-production assembly — timeline composition, transitions, audio production (VO/TTS, BGM), audio mixing, duration enforcement, cover bake-in, and non-generative edits (trim, speed, crop, scale). Use when video segments are ready and need assembling into a finished video, when reassembling after modification-skill re-generates segments, or for non-generative edits (trim, speed, crop, volume) on existing video.

skills_metadata.name: brainstorm-skill
skills_metadata.description: Multimodal creative engine - clarify user intent, validate creative direction, run production-gate checks (format), and write the creative script (narrative arc, key beats, emotional shape, audio direction) for downstream skills to split into executable shots. Use when the user wants to create a video and hasn't provided a full production-ready brief - when creative direction needs developing, format (duration/aspect ratio) is undecided, or the request is a feeling/mood/reference rather than a shot-by-shot plan. Also use when a long narrative script exists but lacks production-level decisions (shot timing, visual style, audio direction).

skills_metadata.name: generation-skill
skills_metadata.description: Execute video segment generation from a confirmed production plan. Handles model routing (Seedance / Kling / Grok - four-layer system), prompt writing, single/multi-sequence generation, and post-generation sanity checks. Produces video segments and hands off to assembly-skill for timeline assembly, audio production (VO/BGM), mixing, and cover. Use when production plan is confirmed and generation is needed.

skills_metadata.name: modification-skill
skills_metadata.description: Self-contained video modification & editing skill - interpret feedback, re-generate segments, directly edit video (trim/speed/crop/volume/transitions), produce and mix audio (VO/BGM), and reassemble. Handles both iterating on Pexo-generated videos AND direct user video editing requests. Routes upstream only when creative direction or production structure needs fundamental changes. Not for first-time creation from scratch (brainstorm/script/generation-skill).

skills_metadata.name: pexo-product-knowledge-skill
skills_metadata.description: Guides the Pexo agent on answering product questions about creation capabilities, credits, pricing, and subscriptions. Defines behavioral principles so the agent never fabricates numbers and redirects gracefully. Use when users ask about video limits, credits, pricing, payment, or subscription management.

skills_metadata.name: script-skill
skills_metadata.description: Sequence-level production design - break a creative script into executable shot sequences with complete visual, audio, editing, and effects design. Handles shot composition, camera language, SFX/dialogue/VO/music planning, visual packaging, and production model routing. Use when creative direction is locked (from brainstorm-skill or user brief) and needs to be translated into a production-ready shot list with per-sequence timing, model routing, and audio design.

skills_metadata.name: subject-asset-skill
skills_metadata.description: Subject element decomposition, user asset organization, reference mapping, gap analysis, and supplementary reference generation. Establishes the complete visual asset foundation before generation begins. Use when a sequence breakdown exists (from script-skill) and user assets need to be organized, gaps identified, or supplementary references generated before generation-skill can execute. Especially important for multi-sequence parallel generation where cross-segment visual consistency depends on reference coverage.

Esta imagem apresenta uma personagem feminina em um estilo de animação 3D moderna e altamente detalhada. Aqui está a descrição detalhada solicitada:

### 1. Estilo Visual
A personagem possui um design característico de **animação 3D de alta qualidade**, semelhante ao estilo de estúdios como Pixar ou Disney moderno. A iluminação é cinematográfica, com um acabamento suave na pele e texturas realistas nos tecidos. O cenário é urbano e noturno, com um efeito de profundidade de campo (fundo desfocado) que destaca a personagem.

### 2. Traços do Rosto e Expressão
*   **Olhos:** São grandes e expressivos, de cor castanho-claro amendoado. Possuem cílios definidos e sobrancelhas bem desenhadas e levemente arqueadas.
*   **Nariz e Boca:** O nariz é pequeno e delicado. Os lábios são finos, com uma coloração rosada natural.
*   **Expressão:** Ela apresenta um olhar sereno, ligeiramente melancólico ou contemplativo, reforçado pela leve inclinação da cabeça.
*   **Formato do Rosto:** Rosto em formato de coração, com queixo delicado e maçãs do rosto suaves.

### 3. Cabelo
*   **Corte:** Curto, estilo "bob" ou "long pixie" repicado, com bastante volume.
*   **Cor:** Castanho-escuro, quase preto.
*   **Detalhes:** O cabelo está repartido lateralmente. É possível notar pequenas gotículas de água (chuva) brilhando nos fios, conferindo realismo à cena.

### 4. Cor da Pele
*   A pele é **clara com subtom quente**, apresentando uma textura macia e uma leve vermelhidão natural nas bochechas e no nariz, sugerindo o clima frio ou úmido do ambiente.

### 5. Roupas e Acessórios
*   **Parte Superior:** Ela veste uma blusa preta justa de gola alta (turtleneck) com mangas de comprimento 3/4.
*   **Parte Inferior:** Calças pretas extremamente ajustadas (estilo skinny ou legging), que marcam a silhueta.
*   **Calçados:** Botas pretas de cano curto, estilo coturno, com cadarços visíveis.
*   **Acessórios:** Um colar fino de prata com um pequeno pingente circular e brincos de argola pequenos e discretos.

### 6. Cores Predominantes
*   **Personagem:** O **preto** é a cor dominante absoluta em seu vestuário, o que cria um contraste forte com sua pele clara.
*   **Ambiente:** A paleta de cores geral é fria e sombria, dominada por tons de **azul-escuro e azul-marinho** (da noite e da chuva).
*   **Acentos:** Há pontos de cor **neon** no fundo (magenta, ciano e amarelo) vindos das luzes da cidade, que se refletem no chão molhado de forma difusa.

     2	name: generation-skill
     3	description: Execute video segment generation from a confirmed production plan. Handles model routing (Seedance / Kling / Grok - four-layer system), prompt writing, single/multi-sequence generation, and post-generation sanity checks. Produces video segments and hands off to assembly-skill for timeline assembly, audio production (VO/BGM), mixing, and cover. Use when production plan is confirmed and generation is needed.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Usage
     7	
     8	**Input**: A locked production plan from script-skill (sequence breakdown, production model, strategy), the per-sequence reference map from subject-asset-skill, optionally a concept preview (with extracted key frames), supplementary reference assets, and optional reference image/video/audio from the user. **Note on images**: All images are plain references - no first-frame/end-frame distinction at the API level; describe first-frame intent in the prompt. **Audio strategy**: Audio co-generation is the #1 priority - SFX and on-screen dialogue are always co-generated in the video generation call, never post-produced. Before generation, every sequence must explicitly declare one primary **audio narrative mode**: `on_camera_sync_speech`, `voiceover_narration`, `silent_broll_with_text`, or `nat_sound_only`. See **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section I (Audio Strategy) and **references/voice-strategy-execution.md** for generation-stage spoken-source hard stops.
     9	
    10	**PREREQUISITE CHECK**: Before starting any generation, verify that the execution strategy is sufficiently specified, regardless of where it came from. At minimum, the following must be clear: hard user constraints, `shot_strategy`, `audio_strategy`, `consistency_strategy`, and `fallback_strategy`. If upstream skills did not provide them explicitly, create a lightweight internal plan before generation. Do not block solely because a specific skill or reference file was not read. Do block or pause if the execution strategy is materially under-specified. Generating sequences without a unified plan produces disjointed, inconsistent video.
    11	
    12	**STORYBOARD CONFIRMATION PROTOCOL** (applies when generation-skill operates directly from user brief - no locked plan from upstream skills):
    13	
    14	When the user provides a brief with reference images and format confirmation, and no upstream plan exists, follow this lightweight confirmation protocol before generating video:
    15	
    16	1. **Present the sequence plan as text** - include the Scene Reference -> Sequence Mapping table (Rule 2) and a one-line description per sequence. Ask if the direction is OK. **Do not generate storyboard images by default** - text descriptions are sufficient for direction alignment. Only generate storyboard key frames if the user explicitly requests visual previews.
    17	
    18	2. **If storyboard images are generated**: Collect feedback. The user may confirm the direction, request scene changes, or flag character appearance issues. **Separate scene direction from character appearance**: if the user's feedback is solely about the character (not the scenes), fix the character reference image once and proceed to video generation - do not regenerate all storyboard frames.
    19	
    20	3. **Maximum 2 confirmation rounds**: After the user has confirmed the scene direction (even implicitly - e.g., feedback is only about character details, not scene content), proceed to video generation. Minor character adjustments (remove accessories, clean up details) should be resolved in a single character reference fix, not through additional storyboard rounds.
    21	
    22	4. **Anti-loop detection**: If 2+ consecutive user messages address only character appearance and not scene direction, the scene direction is implicitly confirmed. Consolidate all character feedback into one reference image fix, then immediately start video generation.
    23	
    24	**Output**: All generated video segments (with their sound-on/off status), plus the Voice Strategy Declaration and BGM Timing Mode Declaration as planning artifacts. These are handed off to **assembly-skill** for timeline assembly, audio production (TTS/BGM), mixing, cover bake-in, and final delivery. **Never expose internal production terms** (sequence numbers, generation modes, sound on/off, model names) to the user - use natural creative language.
    25	
    26	## Degraded Execution Declaration
    27	
    28	When using a non-ideal path due to model or tool limits, record it explicitly in working context before handoff.
    29	
    30	Examples:
    31	
    32	- `degraded_mode: segmented_continuation`
    33	- `degraded_mode: post_produced_voice`
    34	- `degraded_mode: weak_consistency_locking`
    35	
    36	A degraded path is allowed if it does not directly violate hard user constraints. The key requirement is to make the compromise visible so downstream assembly and QA can evaluate it correctly.
    37	
    38	**Constraints & Behavior**:
    39	
    40	1. **Model selection**: Execute using the model recommended by script-skill. The four-layer routing system, tool call mapping, and decision tree are defined in **references/video-models-routing.md** Section I - verify every `video_generate` call against that definitive reference before submission.
    41	   - **Pre-call model verification** (mandatory): Before every `video_generate` call, confirm `provider`, `model`, `mode`, and `provider_param` key all match the routing decision per the mapping table in **references/video-models-routing.md** Section I. Mismatching any field is a critical error.
    42	   - **Reference-discard check**: If user-uploaded reference materials exist and the call uses `mode: "text2video"`, STOP - `text2video` cannot accept `image_list`/`video_list`/`audio_list`. Re-route to Seedance or Kling with `reference2video`.
    43	   - **Image-list population check**: When user-uploaded images exist and the production model supports references, `image_list` MUST contain at least the user's primary reference image.
    44	   - **Sound-off sanity check** (mandatory before every `video_generate` call with `sound: "off"`): Verify that the prompt does NOT describe visible speaking, singing, talking, vocalizing, presenting, or any mouth-movement-producing action. If the prompt contains on-screen dialogue cues (character speaking to camera, talking, singing, announcing, reading aloud, delivering a message, recording a greeting) AND sound is off, this is a **critical error** - the Voice Strategy Declaration was either skipped or incorrectly resolved. STOP, re-run the Voice Strategy Declaration (Rule 2, Steps 1-3), and correct the sound parameter before submitting the call. On-screen dialogue with `sound: "off"` produces decorative lip movements that cannot sync with any post-assembly audio - the result is always an audio-visual mismatch. **This check also applies when replicating a previous project's approach** - prior execution history is reference context, not a substitute for the Voice Strategy Declaration on the current project.
    45	   - **`audio_list` duration-lock check** (mandatory before every `video_generate` call that uses `audio_list` for visible speaking / lipsync): Treat the source audio as the primary clock. Do **not** set `duration` longer than the referenced speech audio. If the model can infer timing from the audio, prefer omitting `duration` rather than forcing a longer whole-second target. If a specific target duration is creatively required, first edit/retime the audio itself to that target and then pass the retimed audio file - never use a 6s speech asset to drive an 8s talking-head clip and then re-attach the original 6s file in assembly.
    46	   - Generation-skill only overrides the model on degradation (see Rule 12).
    47	2. **Build the Production Blueprint**: Break the brief into an executable **Sequence** list. When **Grok** is selected, the plan is a single sequence; write one flowing narrative prompt per Grok's style. Each sequence represents a **self-contained narrative paragraph containing multiple shots** (see **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section III). Duration per sequence depends on the production model: **Seedance <=15s**, **Kling <=10s**, **Grok <=10s**. **Single-call preference** (see **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section II): When total video duration fits within the model's single-call max, strongly prefer generating the entire video in one call - use prompt-internal timing cues (`[0-5s]`, `[5-10s]`, `[10-15s]`) to structure beats within a single prompt. This avoids unnecessary cross-segment consistency risk, redundant API calls, and post-assembly overhead. Split only when there is a clear production reason (independent scenes needing different references, isolated retry needs). For multi-sequence videos, leverage Seedance's 15s cap to reduce sequence count and cross-sequence consistency risk - let narrative rhythm determine natural break points within the model's limit. Plan all sequences upfront before generating any - map the full narrative arc first, then write individual prompts. End at a natural pause point so sequences can chain cleanly.
    48	   - **Shot duration heuristics** - when the sequence includes voiceover or on-screen text:
    49	     - **VO/text coverage**: Budget shot duration >= spoken/read duration + 0.5-1s slack (~3-4 Chinese chars/sec, ~2.5-3 English words/sec). When planning a sequence that hosts voiceover/narration, budget the sequence duration to be **at least** the estimated VO read time + 1s - never shorter. Example: a 20-character Chinese voiceover at 3-4 chars/sec needs 5-7s of speaking time; do not assign it to a 4s sequence. For English VO, treat a 15s target as roughly 35-42 spoken words after pauses/emphasis; denser product explainers must be rewritten before generation. If the narrative structure constrains the sequence to a shorter duration, shorten the VO text to fit the available time.
    50	     - **Single-sequence VO fit gate**: The single-call preference does not override VO fit. If a 15s Seedance video uses post-produced VO, the planned VO copy must fit the 15s target before generation starts. If it does not fit, shorten the copy or revise the duration; do not send an overlong VO plan downstream expecting assembly to trim it.
    51	     - **Audio-driven talking-head exception**: When visible speech is driven by a provided speech asset via `audio_list`, the sequence duration must follow that asset's real duration - not a padded storyboard beat. Small tail room is acceptable only if it is intentionally baked into the audio file itself. Do not plan extra silent hold time after a lipsynced line unless you generate a separate visual-only tail segment.
    52	     - **Breathing room**: ~0.5-1s between narrated shots, ~1.5-2s visual-only between narrated sequences.
    53	     - **Shots without narration** follow emotional weight rather than text timing - see `references/editing-rhythm-design.md` Section 4.
    54	     - Sub-second precision is below model resolution - use timing cues as pacing guidance.
    55	   - **Visual Intent Pass** (multi-sequence only): Before writing any individual prompt, establish a unified visual language using the **Visual Style Convention** (4 constants: rendering style, color palette, lighting mood, texture quality) from the script-skill handoff. These constants become a **style preamble** prepended to every segment's prompt - this prevents each segment from independently interpreting the visual style. Verify adjacent segments for unintentional style drift before writing prompts.
    56	   - **Scene Reference Image Coverage** (mandatory when user provides multiple distinct scene/environment reference images):
    57	
    58	     | Constant | Example | What it controls |
    59	     |----------|---------|-----------------|
    60	     | **Rendering style** | photorealistic / cinematic / painterly / illustration / motion graphics | The fundamental look - mixing styles across segments (e.g., nature macro -> CGI -> studio) is the #1 cause of visual disconnection |
    61	     | **Color palette** | warm golden tones / cool desaturated / neutral with jade accents | Dominant color character - shifts of >2 stops between adjacent segments look like different videos |
    62	     | **Lighting mood** | soft natural / dramatic rim light / studio even / golden hour | Lighting consistency is as important as color - a studio-lit segment adjacent to a natural-light segment breaks immersion |
    63	     | **Texture quality** | organic film grain / clean digital / dreamy soft focus | Surface treatment - gritty next to polished reads as a style error, not variety |
    64	
    65	     These 4 constants become a **style preamble** that is prepended to every segment's prompt. Example: "Cinematic photorealistic look, warm golden palette with jade accents, soft diffused natural lighting, organic film-like texture." This preamble is not optional - it is the mechanism that prevents each segment from independently interpreting the visual style.
    66	
    67	     **Step 2 - Visual Intent Table** - one row per sequence:
    68	
    69	     | Seq | Color Temperature | Shot Anchor | Human Relationship | Transition In | Narrative Justification |
    70	     |-----|-------------------|-------------|--------------------|---------------|-------------------------|
    71	     | ... | ...               | ...         | ...                | ...           | ...                     |
    72	
    73	     Rules for filling the table:
    74	     - Every cell must contain an explicit absolute description (e.g., "cool overcast grey", "wide -> mid-shot", "two workers in conversation"). No cell may be left blank or marked "same as above."
    75	     - Adjacent rows may share the same value when the narrative calls for continuity - but the justification cell must explain why (e.g., "maintains emotional momentum from seq2"). Similarity by default, not by intent, is what this step prevents.
    76	     - Transitions: carry meaning beyond cut/no-cut - note the reason (e.g., "dissolve - 20-year time jump", "cut - same scene, momentum continuity").
    77	     - **Color Temperature** values must be consistent with the Style Convention's color palette. If a segment needs a different temperature (e.g., flashback in cool blue), the Narrative Justification must explain the shift, and the transition must signal it.
    78	     - This table is produced once before any generation call. Because every row is self-contained with absolute values, it works identically for both serial and parallel generation.
    79	
    80	     **Step 3 - Style Drift Check** (validate before writing prompts): Scan the completed table row by row. For each adjacent pair of segments, verify:
    81	     - Would the two segments look like they belong in the same video? If segment A describes "macro nature photography in soft morning light" and segment B describes "CGI particle convergence in dark studio lighting," they will look like clips from two different projects.
    82	     - If a style shift is intentional (e.g., reality -> fantasy transition), the Transition In cell must contain a transition type that signals the shift (dissolve, whiteout, motivated cut) and the Narrative Justification must explain why.
    83	     - If a style shift is unintentional - the segments just ended up with different visual languages because they describe different subjects - **unify them** by rewriting both to share the Style Convention's constants. Different subjects can coexist within one visual language; different visual languages cannot.
    84	
    85	     Prompts are written by translating each row's design decisions into language - not by re-inventing the visual design during prompt writing. **Every prompt starts with the Style Convention preamble**, followed by the segment-specific direction from the table row.
    86	   - **Scene Reference Image Coverage** (mandatory when user provides multiple distinct scene/environment reference images):
    87	     Count the number of distinct scene/environment reference images the user provided (different locations, backgrounds, or settings - not multiple angles of the same scene). The Production Blueprint must **use every user-provided scene reference image** - no image may be silently dropped.
    88	     - **Mapping is flexible**: N scene reference images do NOT require N sequences. A single <=10s sequence can contain multiple scene transitions - pass multiple scene reference images into one sequence's `image_list` and describe the scene cuts in the prompt. Kling handles intelligent scene-splitting from text. Example: 3 scene references in a 10s sequence -> prompt describes a 3-location montage, image_list contains all 3 scene images plus the character reference.
    89	     - **Sequence count is driven by duration and narrative, not reference count**: Plan sequences based on `target_duration / max_sequence_duration` and narrative arc, then distribute scene references across sequences. A 15s video with 4 scene references could be 2 sequences x ~8s (each covering 2 scenes) or 4 sequences x ~4s - the right split depends on pacing and transition design.
    90	     - **Explicit mapping table** (include in plan output to user):
    91	       | Seq | Scene References Used | Planned Duration |
    92	       |-----|----------------------|-----------------|
    93	       | 1   | Image 1 (street), Image 2 (station) | 8s |
    94	       | 2   | Image 3 (bridge), Image 4 (temple) | 8s |
    95	     - If any user-provided scene reference image is not mapped to a sequence, explain why in the plan.
    96	     - This rule supplements, not replaces, the Visual Intent Table - the mapping table is a planning tool; the Visual Intent Table governs visual consistency.
    97	   - **Speed-change segments**: When the creative brief calls for slow-motion or fast-motion within a segment, generate source material at the correct pre-speed duration: source duration = output duration x playback speed. Example: 5s of 0.5x slow-motion needs only 2.5s of source -> generate with duration=3 (round up), then apply `speed=0.5` in edit spec using the full source (`in_ms=0`, omit `out_ms` or set it to the full source duration). Do not generate full-length source and then trim `out_ms` to fit - truncation discards the tail of the action, often the most important moment.
    98	   - **Voice Strategy Declaration** (mandatory before generation - any video with spoken audio): Read `references/voice-strategy-execution.md` before writing generation prompts. Before writing any generation prompt, classify every spoken audio element in the creative brief and assign it to exactly one source. This declaration is binding - once a line is assigned to a source, it cannot also be produced by the other source.
    99	     - **Step 0 - Declare the audio narrative mode per sequence**: Explicitly choose exactly one primary mode for each sequence: `on_camera_sync_speech`, `voiceover_narration`, `silent_broll_with_text`, or `nat_sound_only`.
   100	       - `on_camera_sync_speech`: the visible person/character is intended to speak on screen; the line must come from generated or audio-driven in-scene speech, not a duplicate post-produced VO.
   101	       - `voiceover_narration`: speech is off-screen narration; avoid strong visual speaking cues in the covered shots unless they are intentionally treated as muted B-roll.
   102	       - `silent_broll_with_text`: no spoken layer is planned; meaning is carried by image, music, and/or text.
   103	       - `nat_sound_only`: production sound / ambience / action sound is the primary audio; do not restate the same content via explanatory VO.
   104	       - If a single moment appears to need two conflicting primary modes, STOP and resolve it in script logic before any generation call.
   105	       - **Character-sync contradiction check**: If the original user request or locked plan says the voice should be synced/matched/aligned to a visible character, presenter, host, doctor, teacher, mascot, or demonstrator, `voiceover_narration` is invalid unless the plan explicitly says the narrator is off-screen and the character is intentionally silent B-roll. Do not write "no speech, no dialogue, no voice" into a prompt under that condition. Re-route to `on_camera_sync_speech` with exact lines / `audio_list`, or ask one focused clarification before any `video_generate` call.
   106	     - **Step 1 - Classify each spoken element** into one of: **on-screen dialogue** (character speaks with visible lip movement), **off-screen narration** (voice accompanies visuals, no on-screen lip movement), **inner monologue** (character's internal thoughts, no lip movement), or **SFX/atmosphere** (non-speech sound tied to visual action). Treat user wording as evidence, not as a literal routing command. Words like "voiceover", "narration", "配音", and "口播" often mean only that spoken explanation is desired; they do not by themselves prove the speaker is off-screen. Build a small mental picture before choosing the source: who would the viewer believe is speaking, and does the body or mouth need to feel connected to the words?
   107	       - Visible-performance leaning: presenter, host, doctor, teacher, AI presenter, talking head, mascot, salesperson, streamer, character demonstrating, character pointing while explaining, "make X say", "speaking to camera", "reading aloud", or voice "synced/matched/aligned to the character". These cues usually point to on-screen dialogue/monologue and the co-gen path.
   108	       - Off-screen-narration leaning: no visible speaker, B-roll or product montage, abstract/diagrammatic explanation, narrator explicitly outside the scene, or a long narrator voice that must remain identical across many independent scenes. These cues usually point to TTS.
   109	       - Mixed leaning: a visible character has some performed lines while a separate narrator provides context or transitions. Co-generate the performed lines; reserve TTS for the unseen narrator only.
   110	       - Tie-breaker: when the phrase could mean either character-synced explanation or generic VO, preserve visible performance first. It is better to ask one focused question or choose co-gen for the visible speaker than to suppress speech and later discover the character should have been speaking.
   111	     - **Step 2 - Determine the voice routing** based on on-screen visibility and whether voice identity must be preserved across languages:
   112	      - **On-screen dialogue / monologue** (character visibly speaks - any visual style including 2D animation, illustration, motion graphics, realistic): **Co-generate path.** Include the exact dialogue/monologue in the sequence prompt (`sound: on`), or use `audio_list` when deterministic speech/lipsync is required. Open-ended phrases like "begins speaking naturally" are not a valid spoken-content contract. Co-generation produces lip-synced, emotionally matched voice that is synchronized with the character's visible mouth movements - this cannot be replicated by post-assembly TTS regardless of visual style. Modern video models handle audio-visual co-generation well across all visual styles.
   113	      - **Off-screen narration / voiceover** (no on-screen speaker): **TTS path.** `sound: on` for SFX only in the prompt (no speech). Avoid visible speaking cues; when a presenter/talking-head visual remains on screen, add an explicit speech exclusion such as `"no speech, no dialogue, no voice, no spoken words"`. Narration via `audio_produce` in post-assembly. This gives full voice control (consistent voice ID, pacing, tone) for narration that spans multiple sequences.
   114	       - **Mixed: same video has both on-screen dialogue AND off-screen narration**: **Split path.** On-screen dialogue lines: co-generate in prompts. Off-screen narration: TTS. The voice difference between co-generated dialogue and TTS narration is acceptable - they serve different narrative roles (character voice vs. narrator voice).
   115	       - **Inner monologue with no visible lip movement** (character thinking, no mouth movement): **TTS path.** Treat as off-screen narration since there is no visual speaking action to synchronize with.
   116	       - **Cross-language dubbing with voice preservation** (user wants the target-language speech to keep the same speaker / same character timbre as the source audio): **Reference-voice dubbing path.** Do **not** route this as ordinary generic TTS. First extract or isolate the source speech and treat it as a **voice identity reference anchor**. Then, if tooling supports it, generate the target-language speech with voice-clone / reference-conditioned TTS. If tooling does not support true voice preservation, explicitly tell the user before final delivery - never silently downgrade this request to arbitrary target-language TTS.
   117	     - **Step 3 - Record the declaration** (internal, not shown to user): For each sequence, note the chosen audio narrative mode, which spoken lines go into the prompt (co-generate), which are produced via `audio_produce` (TTS), and which are absent (SFX-only sequences). This declaration feeds directly into prompt writing (Rule 7) and the Assembly Handoff (Rule 10).
   118	     - **Anti-Doubling Hard Stop**: A spoken line MUST have exactly one audio source - enforced at **planning time**, not just assembly time. Before triggering any generation or TTS call, verify that each spoken line is assigned to exactly one source in the Step 3 declaration. If the same line appears in both a generation prompt (co-gen) and an `audio_produce` call (TTS), this is a planning error - cancel one path before any call is made. At assembly time: if both co-generated voice (embedded in video) and a TTS asset exist for the same spoken content, assembly is **blocked**. Remove one source before proceeding. See assembly-skill SKILL.md Rule 1 (DOUBLE-VOICING CHECK).
   119	     - **Dubbing downgrade hard stop**: Requests for "same voice", "same speaker", "same character voice", "keep the original timbre", or "translate this speech into another language but keep the same voice" are **not equivalent** to ordinary narration requests. If the pipeline cannot perform reference-voice dubbing, stop and surface the limitation to the user instead of silently shipping a generic TTS voice.
   120	   - **BGM Timing Mode Declaration** (mandatory for any video with BGM - decide before generation begins): Determine the temporal relationship between music and visuals. This decision affects generation order.
   121	     - **Step 1 - Assess the creative brief's audio-visual relationship**:
   122	       - Does the brief describe specific musical moments tied to visual events (beat drops on scene changes, rhythmic cuts, music swells at emotional peaks)? -> **video-first**: generate video segments first, analyze their actual rhythm, then compose BGM to match.
   123	      - Does the user provide an audio track, or does the brief design the narrative around a musical arc (music video, dance choreography, audio-driven montage)? -> **music-first**: generate or analyze the audio first, then generate video segments with timing informed by the audio. **Current tool boundary**: today's `video-editor__analyze_audio` only gives `duration`, `bpm`, `lufs`, `lufs_range`, and `true_peak` - use it for tempo / loudness inspection, but do **not** assume beat timestamps or segment boundaries exist. **Seedance `audio_list` implementation** (mandatory when Seedance is the production model): pass the user's audio file via the `audio_list` parameter on the `video_generate` call (use the audio asset path returned by upstream tools) - Seedance generates video whose motion and rhythm are reactive to the input audio. This is the core mechanism of music-first mode. Do NOT generate video without `audio_list` and then mix the audio in via `execute_edit_video` - that produces unsynchronized results. When the user says "use the feel of this music" or provides BGM as creative input, this path is triggered.
   124	       - Is the BGM purely ambient atmosphere with no expected sync to visual beats (background texture, mood layer, simple product showcase)? -> **independent**: generate BGM and video in parallel for speed.
   125	     - **Step 2 - Record the mode** (internal): Note the chosen mode and reasoning. This feeds directly into execution order (Rule 5 for multi-sequence generation) and the Assembly Handoff (Rule 10).
   126	     - **Default**: For multi-sequence narrative videos (>10s), default to **video-first** unless the brief explicitly indicates music-led pacing. For single-segment videos (<=10s), default to **independent**. **Exception**: When the user provides an audio track (uploaded BGM/music), default to **music-first** regardless of duration or sequence count.
   127	     - See **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section IV (BGM Planning) for the full framework.
   128	3. **Reference Mapping per Sequence** (mandatory before generation begins): Using the Subject Element Registry from subject-asset-skill, build a **per-sequence reference plan** - which assets go into each sequence's image list, and what role each plays.
   129	   - For each sequence, identify which subject elements from the registry appear in that sequence's narrative.
   130	   - Assign concrete assets: user uploads, concept preview key frames, supplementary generated images. Each asset gets a positional index (`image 1`, `image 2`, ...) that will be referenced in the prompt.
   131	   - **Every image in the image list must be explicitly referenced in the prompt** - declare its role (product_ref, character_ref, style_ref, etc.) and what the model should extract from it. No orphaned references.
   132	   - **Gap filling**: If the registry shows an element as "uncovered" or "text description," write a detailed textual description for it in the prompt. Use character budget on uncovered elements; save budget on covered elements by pointing to reference images instead of re-describing them.
   133	   - **When image slots are limited** (see tool schema for exact capacity per scenario), prioritize: product_ref > character_ref > style_ref > environment_ref > packaging_ref. If a sequence needs more references than the limit allows, combine roles (one image can anchor both product and style) or compress lower-priority elements to text descriptions.
   134	   - **User upload consistency anchor - never text2image what the user already provided**: When the user has uploaded reference images (character, scene, style, product), these images are the **single source of visual truth**. All derived assets must trace back to user uploads to maintain consistency:
   135	     - **Permitted**: Directly use user uploads in `image_list` - highest consistency.
   136	     - **Permitted**: Use `image2image` with a user upload as the source image (e.g., to place the character into a scene, to remove accessories, to adjust framing) - maintains consistency because the source image anchors the visual identity.
   137	     - **Prohibited**: Use `text2image` to regenerate content that a user upload already covers - text descriptions cannot capture the full visual identity of the user's asset, and the model will produce a different interpretation. This applies to both character references and scene references. Even if the prompt describes the user's image in great detail, the text2image output will diverge from the original.
   138	    - **When a referenced asset becomes unresolved**: Refresh the asset metadata/reference via `get_file_info`; do not regenerate the asset via `text2image`. Reference-resolution failures are transient infrastructure issues, not a reason to create a new (inconsistent) version of an existing asset.
   139	  - **Refresh file info before generation calls**: Before issuing any batch of `video_generate` or `image_generate` calls that reference uploaded assets, call `get_file_info` for all referenced assets so the tool sees fresh `file` inputs. Do not rely on stale cached file info - unresolved file paths/inputs can cause avoidable "file not found" failures and unnecessary regeneration.
   140	4. **Single-Sequence (<=10s Kling/Grok, <=15s Seedance)**: Use **create video** with reference images and **audio co-generation enabled** (`sound: "on"` for Seedance, `sound: on` for Kling) to produce video + synchronized audio together - **dialogue, monologue, and SFX/environment/atmosphere** are co-generated. **Music and voiceover/narration may also be co-generated only when the final user-facing output is this one single segment** and there is no expected later assembly, extension, or revision chain. If the segment may later be reused, extended, or assembled into a longer cut, keep music and voiceover in post. **Never split a single-sequence video into multiple calls**. Seedance supports `sound: "on"` even when `image_list`, `video_list`, or `audio_list` are provided - unlike Kling which forces silent output with reference video.
   141	   - **User-provided audio check** (mandatory for single-sequence Seedance): If the user uploaded audio (BGM, music, sound reference) and the production model is Seedance, include the audio file in `audio_list`. Seedance generates video with motion and rhythm reactive to the input audio - this produces superior audio-visual sync compared to mixing the audio in afterward via `execute_edit_video`. When `audio_list` is provided, the prompt should NOT include `"no background music"` - the audio_list IS the music source, and the model should generate visuals synchronized to it.
   142	   - **Key-frame control is optional, not default**: For a single-sequence reference-based video, do **not** automatically generate supplementary key frames. First attempt direct production using the user uploads as `character_ref` / `product_ref` / `scene_ref` and describe the state change in the video prompt.
   143	   - **When a control key frame is justified**: Generate **one** supplementary key frame only when it materially reduces drift risk in a critical beat - e.g. a complex final worn state, assembled product payoff, transformation target state, or another high-stakes end frame whose visual relationship is not directly covered by the user uploads.
   144	   - **Single-sequence key-frame cap**: Default cap is **0-1** supplementary key frames for a single-sequence video. Go beyond one only when multiple distinct high-risk visual states genuinely need independent control.
   145	   - **Reference-led hard rule for supplementary key frames**: If the key frame concerns a subject/product already present in user uploads, the key frame must be derived from those uploads via direct reference inputs (`image2image` / reference-led image generation). **Never** generate that key frame via pure `text2image`.
   146	5. **Multi-Sequence (>15s Seedance / >10s Kling)**: See **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section II for the full parallel/serial decision framework. **Parallel is the default** for speed. Serial is only for continuous unbroken action or same-scene frame-level continuity. Audio is **not** a factor - Seedance supports `sound: "on"` in serial continuation.
   147	   - **User intent overrides**: Explicit requests for fast cuts / montage / multi-angle -> parallel regardless of action type.
   148	   - **Parallel**: All sequences use create video with images only, `sound: "on"`. Sequences generated concurrently with shared reference images.
   149	   - **Serial continuation**: Seedance: pass previous sequence as `video_list`, `sound: "on"`, <=15s. Kling: reference video forces silent - prefer converting to parallel with extracted key frames to preserve audio. Use relative camera motion descriptions across segments.
   150	   - **Tail-frame extraction**: Extract a **static image** (PNG/JPEG) from the sharpest frame in the final ~0.5s - not a video clip. Never pass MP4 into `image_list`. Never AI-regenerate the extracted frame.
   151	   - **Parallel prerequisite - reference completeness check**: Before parallel generation, verify every cross-sequence subject element has a concrete visual reference. `style_ref` only counts for look - it does NOT count as character/environment identity coverage. If any element lacks a reference -> generate it first.
   152	   - **Single-segment fallback**: If one segment fails, fall back only that segment per the degradation chain. Do not switch all remaining segments.
   153	   - **EXECUTION MANDATE**: When parallel mode is selected, **issue all generation calls simultaneously in a single tool-call batch**. Never serialize independent calls. This applies to concept previews and image generation batches too.
   154	   - **Audio handoff**: After all segments are generated, hand off to assembly-skill. SFX and on-screen dialogue are **always co-generated** - never post-produced. Do not re-generate co-generated audio; do not co-generate lines assigned to TTS.
   155	6. **Reference Anchor Input** (when using Seedance or Kling with reference images): If a concept preview exists, **extract a representative key frame as a static image** and treat it as the **`style_ref` for every production sequence** - this is the visual style anchor that establishes color grading, lighting tone, and overall aesthetic. Pass it alongside the `product_ref` / `character_ref` images in every sequence's image_list. **The product reference image alone constrains content (what appears), not style (how it looks) - without the preview frame as style_ref, each sequence will independently interpret the visual style and produce an incoherent look across the video.** Extract the frame at the midpoint of the preview clip (where the visual tone is most established), not from the first or last frame (which may be transitional). **This frame must appear in every sequence's image_list, not just the first.** **Critical**: the image list only accepts image files (JPEG, PNG, WebP) - **never pass a video asset into the image list**; this will cause "Image format is invalid" errors. When only a video asset is available for reference, either: (a) use it as the **reference video** input (feature mode, <=10s), or (b) generate a static key frame image first, then pass the image. Do not pass a Grok-generated video directly as reference to Seedance or Kling - use extracted key frames instead. When references cannot cover all elements, generate supplementary reference images **before** starting generation - strong reference coverage is essential since parallel is the default mode. When using **Grok** for production (pure T2V, no assets), this step does not apply.
   156	   - **Do not over-credit the style anchor**: A preview key frame or generated style frame stabilizes color, lighting, and mood. It does **not** reliably stabilize who the character is, what a recurring room specifically looks like, or how two people relate in a story beat. Treat `style_ref` as necessary but insufficient for story-driven multi-sequence generation.
   157	   - **Single-still bootstrap prohibition**: Do not replace missing `character_ref` / `environment_ref` coverage by generating one generic style still and feeding it to every sequence. That pattern produces globally coherent color but locally generic scenes, drifting faces, and weak payoff shots.
   158	   - **Completed-look key frame interpretation**: A generated or extracted "completed look" key frame is a **control anchor for a specific target state**, not a replacement for the original `character_ref` or `product_ref`. Keep the user uploads in the image list and assign distinct roles in the prompt.
   159	   - **No silent reference break after `get_file_info`**: If `get_file_info` was called in preparation for a supplementary `image_generate`, the next `image_generate` call must actually include the referenced images as tool inputs. Do not refresh file info and then fall back to prompt-only `text2image` for the same covered subject.
   160	7. **Prompt Writing**: Follow **references/video-generation-execution.md** Section III for the full prompt spec (layer priority, syntax per model, character limits, reference-first economy). Key execution rules unique to generation:
   161	   - **Material reference syntax**: Seedance: positional (`"image 1"`, `"video 2"`). Kling: `<filename>`. Grok: `@filename`. Every image in the list must be referenced in the prompt with its role declared.
   162	   - **SFX mandatory check**: Every `sound: on` prompt must contain at least one concrete SFX description tied to a visual action. Generic atmosphere words do not count.
   163	   - **No co-generated BGM**: Every `sound: on` prompt in multi-sequence production must include `"no background music, no musical score, no musical instruments - sound effects and ambient audio only"`. **Exception**: when `audio_list` is provided (music-first mode), do NOT include this exclusion.
   164	   - **SFX coherence** (multi-sequence): Define a shared ambient foundation across all segments. Plan SFX as a designed arc, not random per-segment choices.
   165	   - **Character consistency**: Pass the same reference images to every sequence featuring the character. Describe only motion/expression/pose in prompt - not static visual attributes visible in the reference.
   166	   - **Brand logo avoidance**: Include `"no visible brand logos, no trademark symbols, plain unbranded clothing"` when generating characters with clothing/accessories.
   167	   - **Product scale anchoring**: Every prompt with product-and-person interaction must contain a realistic scale statement.
   168	   - **On-screen text / packaging**: Follow `references/packaging-keyframe-guide.md`. Never ask the video model to typeset readable text from prompt - always use a key frame reference image. Layer 2 elements (precise text) are not supported.
   169	8. **Per-Sequence Duration Enforcement**: When the user provides a shot-by-shot script with explicit per-segment timing (e.g., "[0-2s]", "[2-4s]"), each sequence's generation duration must match the scripted segment duration - **not** the model's default or maximum. After each sequence is generated, verify its actual duration via `ffprobe` or `get_file_info`. If a sequence exceeds the scripted duration, **trim it** in the edit spec (`in`/`out` parameters) to match the user's timing before assembly. Do not silently deliver a video longer than the agreed total - the sum of all trimmed sequences must match the user-confirmed duration (+/-1s tolerance).
   170	9. **Post-Generation Sanity Check** (multi-sequence, same character): After all sequences are generated and before assembly, do a **lightweight correctness check** - not a subjective quality review. Use `analyze_file_content` on one representative frame per sequence (mid-point) and verify only binary pass/fail criteria:
   171	   - **Character present**: Does the character actually appear in the sequence? (Catches cases where the model ignored the reference entirely.)
   172	   - **Gross deformation**: Is the character's body structurally intact? (Catches severe artifacts like missing limbs, extra heads, melted faces - not subtle style drift.)
   173	   - If either check fails on a sequence, re-generate that sequence once with the same reference images. Do not iterate beyond one retry - if the re-generation also fails the check, proceed with the best result and let the user decide.
   174	   - Do **not** check for subjective quality (expression accuracy, motion smoothness, aesthetic preference) - that is the user's judgment, not a gate. The goal is to catch obvious errors without adding meaningful latency to the pipeline.
   175	10. **Assembly Handoff** (after all video segments are generated and sanity-checked): Hand off to **assembly-skill** with:
   176	   - All generated video segments (populate the `file` field with the actual asset file path returned by upstream tools; include each segment's actual duration and sound-on/off status)
   177	   - **Audio lineage per segment** (mandatory): For each segment, declare the audio source - `co-gen` (model generated SFX/dialogue from prompt), `audio_list_tts` (TTS file passed via `audio_list` for lipsync - audio is baked into the video), `audio_list_music` (music file passed via `audio_list`), or `silent` (sound off). This lineage feeds assembly-skill's mandatory AUDIO AUDIT step, which probes each segment before deciding whether to add VO/BGM tracks.
   178	   - Voice Strategy Declaration (which spoken lines are co-generated, which need TTS production, and each sequence's audio narrative mode)
   179	   - **Voice Source Declaration passthrough** (mandatory): carry forward script-skill's per-line declaration, including exact text, `planned_source`, speaker visibility, generation requirement, assembly guard, and `requires_assembly_asr`. If generation changes any source decision, update the declaration before handoff. If a line uses `audio_list_tts`, mark `do_not_add_separate_vo: true`.
   180	   - BGM Timing Mode Declaration (video-first / music-first / independent)
   181	   - Creative script audio direction (VO copy, BGM descriptions, SFX notes)
   182	   - Transition recommendations from the production plan
   183	   - Cover source candidates (concept preview key frames, style_ref images)
   184	   
   185	   Assembly-skill owns: TTS/VO production, BGM production, timeline assembly with transitions, audio mixing and volume management, duration enforcement, cover bake-in, and non-generative edits. **Re-read `assembly-skill/SKILL.md`** before writing any edit spec - the mandatory AUDIO AUDIT, media-fact inspection, and anti-doubling checks cannot be executed from memory. Assembly will verify that any declared BGM plan has a matching music_generate output -- if BGM is planned but not produced, assembly is blocked.
   186	   
   187	   **Explicit voiceover copy is binding**: When the user or creative brief provides actual voiceover/narration lines, those are required deliverables that assembly-skill must produce. Do not let them be silently dropped during handoff. The full spoken content must survive final assembly; if estimated or actual VO duration exceeds the target visual window, handoff must mark assembly as blocked until the VO is regenerated shorter or the visual timeline is extended. Never hand off a plan that depends on trimming VO with `out_ms`.
   188	   
   189	   **No silent downgrade**: If voice or music generation is unavailable or fails, surface the limitation to the user rather than silently delivering an incomplete video.
   190	11. **Scenario Routing**: Route each generation call based on the production model and input. See **references/video-models-routing.md** Section II for model-specific scenarios and capacity limits.
   191	   - **Handoff first**: Start from the upstream production-model choice and only change course when there is a clear degradation reason from Rule 12.
   192	   - **Closeup guidance**: A closeup, hand detail, face detail, product beauty shot, or general precision request does not automatically call for Kling.
   193	   - **Preview continuity**: If the approved preview worked on Seedance and the same stylized identity and reference set remain in use, Seedance is often still the best production route unless a concrete issue appears.
   194	   - **Creating new footage** -> create video. Seedance: `sound: "on"` regardless of reference type. Kling: sound on without reference video; always silent with reference video.
   195	   - **Continuing from a previous sequence** -> Seedance: pass as `video_list` + `sound: "on"` (audio preserved). Kling: pass as reference video (always silent - prefer converting to parallel with ref images if audio must be preserved).
   196	   - **Visual-only fixes** (restyle, re-skin) -> edit video (Kling only) - preserves structure and timing, sound off (can preserve original audio).
   197	   - **Reference video provided by user** -> Seedance: use as `video_list` with `sound: "on"`. Kling: use as reference video, accept silent output.
   198	12. **Fallback & Degradation**: When the selected production model fails, follow the degradation chain in **references/video-models-routing.md** Section III. Key principles:
   199	   - **Audio co-generation must be preserved** - never degrade to post-production SFX or dialogue. If audio co-gen fails: retry with reference images only (extract key frames from video), then change strategy and inform user.
   200	   - **Document the reason before switching models** - if execution moves from Seedance to Kling, note the concrete trigger in the working state before the next `video_generate` call. Reasons like `closeup`, `real face`, `detail`, or `better quality` are usually too vague on their own; valid triggers include copyrighted-IP rejection, readable text/UI requirements, micro-detail accuracy, or a documented Seedance generation failure.

201	   - **Reference preservation is a hard rule** - when converting from reference video to reference images during degradation, always extract key frames from the video or use user originals. Never AI-regenerate. Never lose visual consistency.
   202	   - **Sequence splitting on Kling degradation** - when a Seedance sequence (<=15s) must degrade to Kling (max 10s), split into 2+ Kling-compatible sequences, prefer parallel for audio preservation.
   203	   - **Inform user** on significant mid-production changes - briefly, in natural language, not technical terms.
   204	13. **Image Prompt Preflight** (before every `image_generate` call):
   205	   - **Technical parameters never belong in prompt text**: Do **not** include aspect ratios (`9:16`, `16:9`), pixel sizes (`1920x1080`), quality labels (`4K`, `HD`), hex/RGB color codes, internal IDs, case numbers, or other metadata in the prompt. These tokens are frequently rendered into the image as visible text.
   206	   - **Provider-specific aspect handling is mandatory**: For Seedream, pass only mapped pixel sizes (`"1920x1080"`, `"1080x1920"`, `"1024x1024"`) via `size`; never pass ratio strings. For Gemini, pass ratio strings via `aspect_ratio`; never pass pixel dimensions there. Follow `references/image-generation-guide.md` exactly.
   207	   - **Non-standard aspect ratios** (e.g., 1.91:1, 4:5, 2.35:1): Image generation only supports 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1. When the user requests an unsupported ratio, generate at the closest covering supported ratio and crop to exact target dimensions - see `references/image-generation-guide.md` "Non-Standard Aspect Ratios" for the full strategy. Do not repeatedly regenerate at a standard ratio expecting the model to fill a non-standard canvas.
   208	   - **Natural-language color descriptions only**: Replace `#000840` / `rgb(...)` style values with visual wording like `deep navy blue`, `warm amber`, or `soft jade green`. **This includes hex/RGB values from the user's own input** - when the user's brief specifies colors as hex codes (e.g., "background gradient #A2D2FF -> #B4F23C"), the agent can reason about those values internally (LLMs understand hex -> color mapping), but must translate them to natural descriptions before writing the image prompt (e.g., "soft sky-blue to pale lime-green gradient"). Never copy user-provided hex codes verbatim into image generation prompts.
   209	   - **Final prompt sanity test**: Read the prompt once as if every token might be printed on the final image. If any remaining token would be embarrassing or obviously non-visual when rendered literally, rewrite before calling the tool.
   210	   - **Brand/IP name prohibition in text2image**: Never include trademarked character or brand names (e.g., Labubu, Pop Mart, Hello Kitty, Disney, Sanrio, Pokemon) in `text2image` prompts - these consistently trigger content safety false positives across providers (observed: >60% failure rate with Seedream). Replace with purely visual descriptions. Note: when the user has uploaded the character image, `text2image` should not be used at all per Rule 3 - use `image2image` with the user's upload as the source, or pass the upload directly.
   211	
   212	14. **Asset Organization** (before generation):
   213	   - When assets exceed the tool's capacity limits per scenario, classify material vs. reference, budget material first, compress references to minimum effective dose.
   214	   - **Seedance limits**: <=9 images in `image_list`, <=3 videos in `video_list` (total <=15s), <=3 audios in `audio_list` (total <=15s, requires at least 1 image or video). Seedance also supports audio references - when the user provides BGM or audio, pass as `audio_list` for audio-visual sync.
   215	   - **Kling limits**: <=7 images (no ref video) or <=4 images (with ref video). Only 1 reference video per call, **must be <=10s**. Over-length videos must be trimmed.
   216	   - When the user provides multiple videos, select the most relevant one; extract key frames from others to use as reference images.
   217	   - Rank by role priority from the Subject Element Registry (product_ref > character_ref > style_ref > environment_ref). Keep within limits; silently drop lowest-priority items.
   218	   - Decisions are autonomous - act like an editor curating raw material.
   219	15. This stage focuses on producing video segments - **execute silently**. Never expose internal details to the user: sequence numbers, model names, routing decisions, prompt internals, or pipeline terminology. Use natural creative language for progress updates.
   220	
   221	# Tools
   222	
   223	Tools are provided at runtime. This skill uses: video generation tools (Seedance via `video_generate`, Kling, Grok) for producing video segments, and `image_generate` for supplementary reference images and packaging key frames. Audio production (`audio_produce`, `text_to_music`) and timeline assembly (`execute_edit_video`) are handled by **assembly-skill**.
